title: Report operational effectiveness per completed task
goal: Compare dated effort estimates with observed development spend, time and outcomes using provenance-aware private metadata
acceptance: Report completed task/repository/attempt/client/model/activity scope, evidence provenance, coverage and unknown fields; retain failed/retried/reopened work
Show known tokens and optional priced cost with rate/source/currency/date; never infer money from subscription or elapsed time
Separate elapsed wall time, measured execution/wait time and active effort; union overlapping calendar intervals and label worker sums separately; incomplete jobs remain censored or unknown
Compare with immutable dated pre-work estimate snapshots including units, scope and uncertainty; retain estimate revisions without hindsight replacement
Distinguish failed attempts, infrastructure failures, review findings and confirmed regressions; preserve successful retries and denominators/sample sizes
Count explicitly recorded human interventions by category and measured duration when available; exclude conversation text, personal identities and inferred blame

Provide neutral cross-source fixtures proving deduplication, overlap, partial/missing data, retry and estimate-revision handling; no native source availability or consumer adoption gates generic acceptance
privacy: Private metadata only, no prompts/transcripts/secrets or personal performance ranking. Commit only deliberately reviewed neutral aggregates.
validation: Planning only2026-11-10; existing ledger stores timestamps but report has no duration/estimate/outcome aggregation. Native sources remain T02; no real counts are reconstructed.
2026-11-10:16 focused usage fixtures pass, including immutable estimate/observation/report join, overlap, unknowns, prices, replay and step attribution. No real token or model campaign claimed.
escalation: Unknown telemetry stays unknown; observed incomplete subsets are not comparable full-task totals
Metrics do not prove causality, quality or agent suitability and do not override priority/dependencies/human gates
